verdict_a_runtime_acceptance.reason: No browser or heavy test was launched in this review. The guarded read-only resume must still prove the exact checkpointed Save ID appears in URL history, selected snapshot, and after a fresh panel document reload.

checkpoint.handling: Inspected filesystem metadata only; contents were not opened, and the file was not changed.

evidence: The new history path separates readiness, trusted pointer click, and list/ID wait into distinct stages, so a failure can be attributed without weakening the acceptance predicates.

The two history waits retain only linked/open/error booleans, bounded counts, and whether the exact Save ID is present. The catch exports only a fixed wait label and stage; it does not serialize the full wait state or raw exception.

A checkpoint with an ID sets reserved=true, so Save is skipped. A reserved checkpoint without a valid UUID throws before Save. The checkpoint is keyed to the selected organization ID and exact URL hash. No checkpoint deletion or record cleanup path was found.

Pointer diagnostics come from the shared driver and use fixed categories and geometry; source comments and inspected implementation show no text, attributes, URLs, field values, or screenshots cross into the receipt.
The auth password is read for form fill only; the login catch replaces details with a fixed error. No credential is added to the report. The runtime receipt contains no observed ID or request body.
limitations: The CDP response-body observer intentionally suppresses retrieval errors; the forcing behavior is a bounded wait for a valid real response ID, so failure remains unverified and cannot authorize another Save once the checkpoint is reserved.
This source review cannot establish that the UI actually opens history, renders the checkpointed row, survives reload, or stays within the guarded resource envelope.

verification.source_review: Read commit diff, current runner and shared pointer driver; checked checkpoint metadata without reading its contents.
